entities.name: CVE-2023-3519
entities.evidence: CVE-2023-3519, an unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting NetScaler (formerly Citrix) Application Delivery Controller (ADC) and NetScaler Gateway.

entities.name: Exploit public-facing application
entities.evidence: exploit of CVE-2023-3519

entities.name: CVE-2023-3519
entities.evidence: CVE-2023-3519 is an unauthenticated RCE vulnerability affecting the following versions of NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway:

entities.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
entities.evidence: In July 2023, a critical infrastructure organization reported to CISA that threat actors may have exploited a zero-day vulnerability in NetScaler ADC to implant a webshell on their non-production NetScaler ADC appliance.

entities.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Bash
entities.evidence: The actors used the webshell for AD enumeration [T1016] and to exfiltrate AD data [TA0010].

entities.name: Data from Local System
entities.evidence: The actors used the decrypted AD credential to query the AD via ldapsearch.

entities.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
entities.evidence: Exfiltrated collected data by uploading as an image file [T1036.008] to a web-accessible path [T1074]

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: The actors attempted to: • Execute a subnet-wide curl command to identify what was accessible from within the network as well as potential lateral movement targets.

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: Verified outbound network connectivity with a ping command (ping -c 1 google.com) [T1016.001].

entities.evidence: [T1074]: cp /var/tmp/test.tar.gz /netscaler/ns_gui/vpn/medialogininit.png.

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: The actors’ other discovery activities were unsuccessful due to the critical infrastructure organization’s deployment of their NetScaler ADC appliance in a segmented environment.

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: The actors attempted to: • Execute a subnet-wide curl command to identify what was accessible from within the network as well as potential lateral movement targets.

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: • Verified outbound network connectivity with a ping command (ping -c 1 google.com) [T1016.001].

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: • Executed host commands for a subnet-wide DNS lookup.

entities.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Command History
entities.evidence: The actors also attempted to delete their artifacts [TA0005]. The actors deleted the authorization configuration file (/etc/auth.conf)—likely to prevent configured users (e.g., admin) from logging in remotely (e.g., CLI) [T1531].

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: To regain access to the ADC appliance, the organization would normally reboot into single use mode, which may have deleted artifacts from the device; however, the victim had a Secure Shell (SSH) key readily available that allowed them into the appliance without rebooting it.

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: The actors’ post-exploitation lateral movement attempts were also blocked by network-segmentation controls. The actors implanted a second webshell on the victim that they later removed. This was likely a PHP shell with proxying capability.

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: The actors likely used this to attempt proxying SMB traffic to the DC [T1090.001] (the victim observed SMB connections where the actors attempted to use the previously decrypted AD credential to authenticate with the DC from the ADC via a virtual machine).

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: Firewall and account restrictions (only certain internal accounts could authenticate to the DC) blocked this activity.

entities.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Web Shell
entities.evidence: Update September 6, 2023: Victim 2 Threat actors uploaded a PHP webshell *logouttm.php* [T1036.005], likely as part of their initial exploit chain, to */netscaler/ns_gui/vpn/. Within an hour of installing the webshell, the actors implanted an Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) binary pykeygen that set user unique identifier (UID) to root and executed /bin/sh [T1059.004] via setuid and execve syscall.* [T1106]. Note: A third party also observed threat actors use an ELF binary (named pip4) to execute /bin/sh via syscall and change the UID to root. pip4 was located at /var/python/bin.

entities.name: Data from Local System
entities.evidence: With root level access, the actors used hands-on-keyboard for discovery. They queried the AD via ldapsearch for users, groups, and computers. They collected the data in gzipped text files renamed 1.css and 2.css and placed the files in /netscaler/ns_gui/vpn/ for exfiltration.

entities.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Command History
entities.evidence: After exfiltrating the files, the actors deleted them from the system [T1070.004] as well as some access logs, error logs, and authentication logs [T1070.002].

entities.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
entities.evidence: For command and control (C2), the actors appeared to use compromised pfSense devices [T1584]; the victim observed communications with two pfSense IP addresses indicating the actor was using them for multi-hop proxying C2 traffic [T1090.003].
